feature_notes: Head section headers are markdown '## Name: task ...'; a '## ' line only starts a head when the text before its first colon resolves through HydraRoster.index(named:), so a head's own '## ' headings stay inside its body

Trailing parenthesised groups on a header are peeled right-to-left and treated as metadata only when: lowercased == "failed", lowercased hasPrefix "stopped", the group contains a decimal digit, or the group is in the effort set {"low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max", "minimal", "fast", "default"}; otherwise peeling stops and the rest is the task
Effort groups are joined with " \u00b7 " and, inside a group, ", " is replaced with " \u00b7 "; efforts are inserted at index 0 so original left-to-right order is preserved
Landing line prefixes recognized: "Landed in your checkout:", "Did not land", "Changed nothing.", "Nothing landed"
"Nothing landed ... in its copy at <path>" yields .unfinished(copyPath:) with a trailing period stripped; the marker searched for is the literal "in its copy at "
"Did not land (<error>): <files>" parses the parenthesised error; an empty error becomes nil
File item regex literal: ^(\\S+) \\(\\+(\\d+) [\u2212\\-](\\d+)\\)( with conflicts)?$ ; the lead writes U+2212 but ASCII hyphen also matches
Before splitting on ", ", these tails are stripped by regex, longest first: "; \\d+ build-output files? (was|were) left out$" then ", and \\d+ more$"; a trailing "." is stripped first

The lead's closing instructions are dropped from the LAST head's body only: the final paragraph (after the last blank-line break) is removed if it starts with any of "The changes listed above", "The heads worked in your checkout", "A file listed with conflicts", "Do not check any of this", "Do not wait for", "A head that failed", "A head the user stopped", "The user queued", "The user sent"

One head: header carries the head, the card is not collapsible, its report is expanded and its blocks parsed synchronously in init; several heads: cards are collapsible, start collapsed, and bodies warm in the background
Totals line format: "<N> head(s)" and, when any files, " \u00b7 <F> file(s) \u00b7 +<A> \u2212<D>"; files line for a single head: "<F> file(s) \u00b7 +<A> \u2212<D>"
The intro sentence containing the literal substring "still at work" is extracted from the character after the previous "." to the end of the intro and shown under the title
cleanedTitle removes repeated "Name: " or "Name " prefixes while at least two remain, leaving exactly one; withoutNamePrefix removes a single leading "Name: "
hasReport is false when the body is empty or exactly "No report."
Persona lookup order for a head: match in the passed personas by name, else HydraRoster.persona(named:), else HydraRoster.persona(at: 0)
Outcome to HydraHeadInfo.Status mapping for the glyph: done -> .completed, failed -> .failed, stopped -> .stopped
unresolved_questions: Chrome.overlay(_:), PopoverScroll, MarkdownView.warm and the chatZoom environment key are defined in other files, so their exact semantics (scroll clamping, warm cache keying) are not established here
The exact lead prompt that generates these report strings is not in this file, so whether every landing phrasing is covered by landingPrefix cannot be confirmed from here

HydraRunMetrics.HeadTiming (id: UUID, personaIndex, name, status, queue, startup, execution, landing: Phase?)
private struct HydraRunMetricsCard: View, Equatable (== compares metrics only)

@MainActor enum with a @MainActor closure parameter headTurns

ui_elements: Card root VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10), .padding(14), .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)

Subtitle (verbatim): "This conversation's lead and heads, as their turns reported it" size 11 secondaryText, fixedSize vertical

Total text: "Not recorded" when nothing recorded; else "<UsagePanel.tokens(n)> tokens", plus " or more" when isPartial

Scope text: "Loading history\u2026" when hasUnloadedHistory; "None yet" when turns == 0; "Not recorded" otherwise when tokens nil; else "<tokens> tokens" plus " \u00b7 <turnsWithUsage> of <turns> turns" when partial

Group row HStack(spacing: 6): ProviderIcon size 11 tinted secondaryText, model name size 11 secondaryText lineLimit(1) truncationMode(.middle), Spacer(minLength: 8), token count size 11 monospacedDigit secondaryText, .padding(.leading, 18); accessibility label "<scope>, <model>, <tokens> tokens"
"Head timings" section header size 12 medium primaryText preceded by a Divider(), shown only when hasTimings

Timing row: VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 3); HStack(spacing: 6) with HydraGlyph size 14 (isRunning when status == .running), name size 12 primaryText lineLimit(1), MiniSpinner() while running, Spacer(minLength: 8); phase text size 11 monospacedDigit secondaryText, .padding(.leading, 20); accessibility label "<name>, <phase text>"
Phase text format: "Queue <t> \u00b7 Startup <t> \u00b7 Run <t>" plus " \u00b7 Landing <t>" when a landing phase exists
Phase text values: RelativeTime.duration(max(0, seconds)), "in progress", "unavailable"
Notes VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 3), each note size 10.5 secondaryText fixedSize vertical
feature_notes: Note always shown: "Totals cover the conversation and its retained heads, not one run. Providers may omit usage for some requests."
Note when isPartial: "Some turns recorded no usage, so the totals are lower bounds."
Note when spansProviders: "Recorded across providers, so the total guides rather than bills."
Note when hasTimings: "Heads work at the same time, so their durations overlap and are not added up."
Scope.isPartial is true when hasUnloadedHistory, or (tokens == nil ? turns > 0 : turnsWithUsage < turns)
recordedTokens is nil only when both lead and heads recorded nothing; otherwise the present side(s) are summed
spansProviders is true when the set of providers across lead.groups + heads.groups has more than one element
Group id is built as "<provider.rawValue>|<model or empty string>"; merging sums tokens per id
Groups sort biggest tokens first, ties broken by ascending id
A head whose runtime is missing or still loading history sets headScope.hasUnloadedHistory = true and contributes no turns

Head timing is read only from HydraHeadInfo boundaries: queue = startedAt - queuedAt (only when queuedAt exists); startup = executionStartedAt - startedAt; execution = phase(executionStartedAt -> executionFinishedAt); landing is nil unless landingStartedAt or landingFinishedAt exists
phase(from:to:isRunning:): nil start -> .unavailable; nil end -> .running when isRunning (status == .running) else .unavailable; both -> .measured(end - start)
Metrics are deliberately conversation-scoped, never per-run, because a continued request lands on a following turn (documented rationale in the file header comment)
Nothing here reads a live cumulative counter, so the text only changes when a turn records new usage rather than per streamed token
modelName falls back through: providers' shortName for the model, then the raw model string, then provider.displayName
The card is Equatable on metrics alone and used with .equatable(), so unrelated panel redraws do not rebuild it

ClosePanelPopover: PopoverSectionHeader "Stop this helper?"; PopoverNote "\u201c<title>\u201d is still working. Closing the panel stops its turn. What it has done so far stays, and its chat moves to the sidebar under this one."; PopoverItem "Close and stop" symbol "stop.circle" isDestructive true; PopoverItem "Keep it working" symbol "arrow.uturn.backward" with an empty action; .frame(width: 300)
PanelResizeGrips: edge strip thickness 6, corner square 16x16; help text "Drag to resize \u00b7 Double-click for the automatic size"; accessibility label "Drag to resize"
PanelDragHandleView drag slop: 2 points before a press becomes a drag
feature_notes: A Hydra head panel shows HydraHeadProgress (task plus progress bar) instead of its transcript when thread.isHydraHead and settings.hydraShowsHeadDetails is false; a user's own helper always keeps its conversation
Closing a panel whose turn is running opens the confirmation popover first (arrowEdge .bottom); closing an idle panel calls close() immediately
sitsBesideComposer: pane.width - 2*20 - panelWidth - 12 >= 360; otherwise the panel docks above the composer and composerReserve is 0
fitsBothSides: pane.width - 2*20 - 2*(panelWidth + 12) >= 360; below that, panels dock on one side only (comment points at PanelScene.lockedSide)

dockedOrigin when beside the composer centres the composer in the row left after both reserves: row = pane.width - reserve.leading - reserve.trailing, composerWidth = min(820, row - 40), composerLeft = reserve.leading + (row - composerWidth)/2; leading panel at composerLeft - 12 - panelWidth, trailing at composerLeft + composerWidth + 12
dockedOrigin when not beside the composer: x = 20 for leading, pane.width - 20 - panelWidth for trailing
dockedOrigin y: Chrome.contentTopInset for a top corner, else pane.height - (sitsBesideComposer ? 14 : composerAreaHeight + 12) - panelHeight

dockCorner hysteresis: the centre must be more than 56 points past the pane middle on an axis to change side or top/bottom, otherwise the current corner is kept; the middle's y is (docks.topLeading.y + docks.bottomLeading.y + panelHeight)/2

PanelDocks.stacked spreads a side's slots evenly between the top and bottom docked y; step = (bottomLeading.y - topLeading.y)/(slots-1); a top-corner panel with below = b sits at slot b, a bottom-corner one at slot slots-1-b; x comes from the corner itself
PanelDocks.corner(forSlot:of:side:): slots with index <= (slots-1)/2 go to the side's top corner with below = index, the rest to the bottom corner with below = slots-1-index
slotIndex rounds (origin.y - topLeading.y)/step and clamps to 0...slots-1; returns 0 when step <= 0
Drag velocity is an exponential blend: velocity = 0.4*previous + 0.6*instant, and readings closer together than 0.004 s are ignored as same-frame events

Flick: release() returns position + velocity * 0.12 (flickCarry), unless at least 0.08 s (restBeforeDrop) has passed since the last move, in which case the panel drops exactly where it is; nil when never moved

PanelPlacement animates with Chrome.panelSlide only when settling: drag.position == nil, not resizing and not in a window live resize; otherwise animation is nil so the panel tracks the pointer and the live resize exactly; both origin and size are animated
SubagentPanel .animation(nil, value: liveResize.isActive) keeps the frame following the pane every live-resize frame

Resize grips sit on the two edges away from the dock corner; the free corner's cursor is the opposite of the dock corner (topLeading -> bottomRight, topTrailing -> bottomLeft, bottomLeading -> topRight, bottomTrailing -> topLeft)
Double-clicking a grip calls onReset (back to the automatic size); the double click fires in mouseDown on clickCount == 2
PanelDragHandleView.acceptsFirstMouse returns true so the first click takes hold even when the window is not key, and mouseDownCanMoveWindow is false so a press moves the panel rather than the window

The working box shows the sending pulse for about 0.9 s after isRunning turns true, then settles into "<name> working"; both state changes animate with Chrome.panelSlide unless a live resize is active
fitted(_:) clamps a dragged size: width through panelWidth's own clamp, height to max(minHeight, min(size.height, panelHeight computed at that width with unbounded preferred height))
compact mode forces the ideal height to 280 while still honouring the dragged width
PanelDragState.reclamp only writes when the stored position is actually outside the pane, so a live resize does not churn observation
PanelDockCorner.acrossTheColumn maps each corner to the one on the other side at the same edge
